source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֤ל הַשֵּׁנִי֙ לְשִׁמְע֔וֹן לְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְע֖וֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָ֑ם וַֽיְהִי֙ נַֽחֲלָתָ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ נַחֲלַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came out the lot the second for Simeon, for [the] tribe of [the] sons of Simeon by their clans; and was their inheritance in [the] midst of [the] inheritance of [the] sons of Judah.

en.L: And the second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon by their clans, and their inheritance was in the midst of the inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah.
en.B: The second lot came out for the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan. Their inheritance lay inside the inheritance of the tribe of Judah.
en.R: The second lot was drawn for the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan. Their share of land was inside the land of the tribe of Judah.

sw.L: Na kura ya pili ikamtokea Simeoni, kabila la wana wa Simeoni kufuatana na koo zao, na urithi wao ulikuwa katikati ya urithi wa wana wa Yuda.
sw.B: Kura ya pili ilitoka kwa kabila la Simeoni, ukoo kwa ukoo. Urithi wao ulikuwa ndani ya urithi wa kabila la Yuda.
sw.R: Kura ya pili ilipigwa kwa ajili ya kabila la Simeoni, ukoo kwa ukoo. Sehemu yao ya nchi ilikuwa ndani ya nchi ya kabila la Yuda.

es.L: Y salió la segunda suerte para Simeón, para la tribu de los hijos de Simeón conforme a sus clanes; y su heredad estuvo en medio de la heredad de los hijos de Judá.
es.B: La segunda suerte salió para la tribu de Simeón, clan por clan. Su heredad quedaba dentro de la heredad de la tribu de Judá.
es.R: La segunda suerte se echó para la tribu de Simeón, clan por clan. Su parte de la tierra estaba dentro de la tierra de la tribu de Judá.

decisions.choice: the second lot: the second of the seven lots cast at Shiloh
decisions.reason: Joshua had men survey the land still to be divided and write it down in seven parts, and then he cast lots for them before the LORD at Shiloh (18:1-10). The first lot fell to Benjamin (18:11). Casting lots left the choice to God (Proverbs 16:33), so each tribe received its land as his gift and not by its own claim. This chapter gives the other six lots in turn.

decisions.choice: in the midst of the inheritance of Judah: Simeon has no region of its own
decisions.reason: Simeon's towns lie inside the southern part of Judah's land, and most of them already appear in Judah's list (15:26-32, 42). Verse 9 gives the reason. Behind it stands Jacob's word about Simeon and Levi: "I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel" (Genesis 49:7).

decisions.choice: inheritance: land given to a family as a lasting possession
decisions.reason: The word names property that passes down within a family from one generation to the next. Israel's land was divided among tribes, clans and families as a gift from God that was to stay in the family (Numbers 26:52-56; 27:1-11). It was received, not earned or bought.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan
alternatives: the tribe of the descendants of Simeon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the tribe of the sons of Simeon by their clans". Literal keeps "sons" with the gender setting, since the tribe was its men, women and children. Balanced and Readable say "the tribe of Simeon", since "sons of Simeon" is simply the tribe's name, and "clan by clan", since the land was shared out among the clans within the tribe. The same wording is used for every tribe in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the lot was drawn; share of land
decisions.reason: Readable says the lot "was drawn" and calls the inheritance a "share of land", which young readers can picture. It does so for every tribe in this chapter.

decisions.choice: "salió la suerte" (L, B); "se echó la suerte" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the lot "came out", as from the vessel in which the lots were shaken; Literal and Balanced keep that, and Readable says the lot was cast for the tribe, as the English Readable says "was drawn". The same opening returns for each of the seven tribes in this chapter.

en.L: And there was for them in their inheritance Beersheba, and Sheba, and Moladah,
en.B: Their inheritance included Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,
en.R: Their land included Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,

sw.L: Na walikuwa nayo katika urithi wao Beer-sheba, na Sheba, na Molada,
sw.B: Urithi wao ulijumuisha Beer-sheba, Sheba, Molada,
sw.R: Nchi yao ilijumuisha Beer-sheba, Sheba, Molada,

es.B: Su heredad incluía Beerseba, Seba, Molada,
es.R: Su tierra incluía Beerseba, Seba, Molada,

decisions.choice: Sheba: kept as in the Hebrew text, though it may repeat the end of the name before it
decisions.reason: With Sheba the list in verses 2-6 has fourteen names, but verse 6 counts thirteen. The same list in 1 Chronicles 4:28 has "Beersheba, Moladah" with no Sheba, and Judah's list has Shema next to Moladah (15:26). Sheba may be a copyist's repeat of the second half of "Beersheba", or another name for Shema. The "and" before it can also be read as "that is", making Sheba a short name for Beersheba itself. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: the chief town of the far south
decisions.reason: Beersheba was linked with Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 21:31-33; 26:23-33) and marked the southern limit of Israel in the saying "from Dan to Beersheba" (Judges 20:1).

decisions.choice: included
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens the list with "and there was for them in their inheritance". Balanced and Readable say "included". The list runs on to verse 6, so each of these verses ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: Ziklag; Beth-marcaboth and Hazar-susah
decisions.reason: Ziklag was later given to David by the Philistine king of Gath (1 Samuel 27:6). Beth-marcaboth means "house of chariots" and Hazar-susah "village of horses"; in the places where Judah's list has Madmannah and Sansannah (15:31), and they may be other names for the same towns.

records.literal_gloss: and Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: cities thirteen and their villages;

en.L: and Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen cities and their villages,
en.B: Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen towns and their villages,
en.R: Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen. In all, there were thirteen towns with their villages.

es.B: Bet-lebaot y Saruhén: trece poblaciones y sus aldeas;
es.R: Bet-lebaot y Saruhén. En total, eran trece pueblos con sus aldeas.

decisions.choice: cities and their villages: towns with the open settlements that belonged to them
decisions.reason: The word for "city" is used for any lasting settlement, from a walled town to a small one, and most of these were small. The "villages" were unwalled settlements, farms and hamlets around a town that depended on it (Leviticus 25:31). "Their villages" means the villages of these towns.

decisions.choice: thirteen: the total of the list
decisions.reason: The count agrees with the list if Sheba is not counted as a separate town (see verse 2).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "cities", the usual word. Balanced and Readable say "towns", since "city" suggests a large place. The same is done through the chapter.

decisions.choice: In all, there were ... with their villages
decisions.reason: Readable closes the list with a short sentence of its own. It does the same with each total in the chapter.

en.B: and also Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four towns and their villages,

sw.L: Aini, Rimoni, na Etheri, na Ashani: miji minne na vijiji vyake,

es.R: También incluía Aín, Rimón, Éter y Asán. En total, eran cuatro pueblos con sus aldeas.

decisions.choice: Ain, Rimmon: two towns
decisions.reason: In Nehemiah 11:29 the name appears as one town, En-rimmon. Here the count of four requires two, as also in Judah's list (15:32).

decisions.choice: a second group of towns
decisions.reason: Ether and Ashan are listed with Judah's towns in the western foothills (15:42), so Simeon's towns lay in two areas: the Negev in the south and a smaller group to the north-west.

decisions.choice: and also / It also included
decisions.reason: The Hebrew starts the second list with no joining word. Balanced adds "and also" to tie it to the first list, and Readable starts a new sentence.

source.text: וְכָל־הַֽחֲצֵרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר סְבִיבוֹת֙ הֶֽעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עַד־בַּֽעֲלַ֥ת בְּאֵ֖ר רָ֣אמַת נֶ֑גֶב זֹ֗את נַחֲלַ֛ת מַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְע֖וֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃

en.B: together with all the villages around these towns, out to Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan.
en.R: It also included all the villages around these towns, as far as Baalath-beer, which is Ramah in the Negev, the dry land in the south. This was the share of land that the tribe of Simeon received, clan by clan.

sw.L: na vijiji vyote [vilivyokuwa] kandokando ya miji hii, hadi Baalath-beeri, Rama ya Negebu. Huu [ndio] urithi wa kabila la wana wa Simeoni kufuatana na koo zao.

es.L: y todas las aldeas que [estaban] alrededor de estas ciudades, hasta Baalat-beer, Ramá del Néguev. Esta [es] la heredad de la tribu de los hijos de Simeón conforme a sus clanes.
es.B: junto con todas las aldeas alrededor de estas poblaciones, hasta Baalat-beer, Ramá del Néguev. Esta fue la heredad de la tribu de Simeón, clan por clan.
es.R: También incluía todas las aldeas alrededor de estos pueblos, hasta Baalat-beer, que es Ramá del Néguev, la tierra seca del sur. Esta fue la parte de la tierra que recibió la tribu de Simeón, clan por clan.

decisions.choice: Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev: two names for one place
decisions.reason: The second name explains the first. "Ramah" means "height". The place may be the Ramoth of the Negev to which David sent gifts (1 Samuel 30:27). It marks the farthest point of Simeon's villages.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry country of the south
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry land south of the hill country of Judah, around Beersheba, where rain is scarce and towns stand by wells.

decisions.choice: This was the inheritance ...: the closing words for each tribe
decisions.reason: Each tribe's section ends with this summary (verses 16, 23, 31, 39, 48).

decisions.choice: which is ...; the dry land in the south
decisions.reason: Readable says that the two names are one place and explains the Negev, as the meaning decisions describe.

source.text: מֵחֶ֨בֶל֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה נַחֲלַ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֑וֹן כִּֽי־הָיָ֞ה חֵ֤לֶק בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָה֙ רַ֣ב מֵהֶ֔ם וַיִּנְחֲל֥וּ בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְע֖וֹן בְּת֥וֹךְ נַחֲלָתָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: From [the] portion of [the] sons of Judah [was the] inheritance of [the] sons of Simeon, for was [the] portion of [the] sons of Judah too great for them; and received inheritance [the] sons of Simeon in [the] midst of their inheritance.

en.L: From the portion of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah [was] the inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon, for the portion of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah was too great for them, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon received an inheritance in the midst of their inheritance.
en.B: The inheritance of the tribe of Simeon came out of the share of the tribe of Judah, because Judah's share was too large for them. So the tribe of Simeon received its inheritance inside Judah's.
en.R: The land of Simeon was taken from Judah's share, because Judah had more land than it needed. So the tribe of Simeon received land inside the land of Judah.

sw.L: Kutoka fungu la wana wa Yuda [ulikuwa] urithi wa wana wa Simeoni, kwa maana fungu la wana wa Yuda lilikuwa kubwa mno kwao, na wana wa Simeoni wakapokea urithi katikati ya urithi wao.
sw.B: Urithi wa kabila la Simeoni ulitoka katika fungu la kabila la Yuda, kwa sababu fungu la Yuda lilikuwa kubwa mno kwao. Hivyo kabila la Simeoni lilipokea urithi wake ndani ya urithi wa Yuda.
sw.R: Nchi ya Simeoni ilichukuliwa kutoka katika fungu la Yuda, kwa sababu Yuda walikuwa na nchi kubwa kuliko walivyohitaji. Kwa hiyo kabila la Simeoni lilipokea nchi ndani ya nchi ya Yuda.

es.L: De la porción de los hijos de Judá [fue] la heredad de los hijos de Simeón, porque la porción de los hijos de Judá era demasiado grande para ellos; y los hijos de Simeón recibieron heredad en medio de su heredad.
es.B: La heredad de la tribu de Simeón salió de la parte de la tribu de Judá, porque la parte de Judá era demasiado grande para ellos. Así la tribu de Simeón recibió su heredad dentro de la de Judá.
es.R: La tierra de Simeón se tomó de la parte de Judá, porque Judá tenía más tierra de la que necesitaba. Así que la tribu de Simeón recibió tierra dentro de la tierra de Judá.

decisions.choice: portion: the part measured out
decisions.reason: This is a different word from "inheritance". It means a share or part that has been measured out, here the land first marked out for Judah (15:1-63).

decisions.choice: too great for them; their inheritance: Judah's
decisions.reason: "Them" and "their" are the people of Judah: their land was more than they could fill and hold, so part of it went to Simeon. Judah's share was the largest of all (chapter 15).

decisions.choice: more land than it needed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "too great for them" means.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַל֙ הַגּוֹרָ֣ל הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לִבְנֵ֥י זְבוּלֻ֖ן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם וַיְהִ֛י גְּב֥וּל נַחֲלָתָ֖ם עַד־שָׂרִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And came up the lot the third for [the] sons of Zebulun by their clans; and was [the] border of their inheritance as far as Sarid.

en.L: And the third lot came up for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Zebulun by their clans. And the border of their inheritance was as far as Sarid.
en.B: The third lot came up for the tribe of Zebulun, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
en.R: The third lot was drawn for the tribe of Zebulun, clan by clan. Their border reached as far as Sarid.

sw.L: Na kura ya tatu ikapanda kwa wana wa Zabuloni kufuatana na koo zao. Na mpaka wa urithi wao ulikuwa hadi Saridi.
sw.B: Kura ya tatu ilitoka kwa kabila la Zabuloni, ukoo kwa ukoo. Mpaka wa urithi wao ulifika hadi Saridi.
sw.R: Kura ya tatu ilipigwa kwa ajili ya kabila la Zabuloni, ukoo kwa ukoo. Mpaka wao ulifika hadi Saridi.

es.L: Y subió la tercera suerte para los hijos de Zabulón conforme a sus clanes. Y la frontera de su heredad fue hasta Sarid.
es.B: La tercera suerte salió para la tribu de Zabulón, clan por clan. La frontera de su heredad llegaba hasta Sarid.
es.R: La tercera suerte se echó para la tribu de Zabulón, clan por clan. Su frontera llegaba hasta Sarid.

decisions.choice: came up: the lot was drawn out
decisions.reason: Lots were drawn from a container or the fold of a garment, so a lot could be said to "come up" or "come out" (verse 1; Leviticus 16:9). The two verbs describe the same act.

decisions.choice: Zebulun's land and its starting point, Sarid
decisions.reason: Zebulun lay in the hills of lower Galilee, north of the Jezreel Valley, between Asher on the west and Naphtali on the east. Sarid, whose site is not certain, was on its southern edge; from there the border is traced first west (verse 11) and then east (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the tribe of Zebulun, clan by clan
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: וְעָלָ֨ה גְבוּלָ֧ם׀לַיָּ֛מָּה וּמַרְעֲלָ֖ה וּפָגַ֣ע בְּדַבָּ֑שֶׁת וּפָגַע֙ אֶל־הַנַּ֔חַל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י יָקְנְעָֽם׃

en.L: And their border goes up westward, and [to] Maralah, and touches Dabbesheth, and touches the wadi that [is] opposite Jokneam.
en.B: Their border goes up westward to Maralah, reaches Dabbesheth, and reaches the wadi that faces Jokneam.
en.R: Their border went up to the west, to Maralah. It reached Dabbesheth and the stream valley near Jokneam.

sw.L: Na mpaka wao unapanda kuelekea magharibi, na [hadi] Marala, na kugusa Dabeshethi, na kugusa korongo lililo mkabala na Yokneamu.
sw.B: Mpaka wao unapanda kuelekea magharibi hadi Marala, unafika Dabeshethi, na kufika kwenye korongo linaloelekeana na Yokneamu.
sw.R: Mpaka wao ulipanda kuelekea magharibi hadi Marala. Ulifika Dabeshethi na bonde la mkondo karibu na Yokneamu.

es.L: Y sube su frontera hacia el occidente, y [a] Marala, y toca Dabeset, y toca el torrente que [está] frente a Jocneam.
es.B: Su frontera sube hacia el occidente hasta Marala, llega a Dabeset y llega al torrente que está frente a Jocneam.
es.R: Su frontera subía hacia el oeste, hasta Marala. Llegaba a Dabeset y al valle del arroyo cerca de Jocneam.

decisions.choice: westward and Maralah: westward, as far as Maralah

decisions.choice: wadi: a stream bed that fills in the rainy season

decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

en.L: And their territory was Helkath, and Hali, and Beten, and Achshaph,
en.B: Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,

sw.R: Nchi yao ilijumuisha Helkathi, Hali, Beteni, Akshafu,

es.B: Su territorio incluía Helcat, Halí, Betén, Acsaf,
es.R: Su tierra incluía Helcat, Halí, Betén, Acsaf,

decisions.choice: border: here the territory
decisions.reason: As in verse 18, the word here names the territory, since a list of towns follows. From verse 26 the passage traces a line again.

decisions.choice: Helkath and Achshaph
decisions.reason: Helkath became a Levite town (21:31). The king of Achshaph had joined the alliance against Joshua in the north (11:1; 12:20).

decisions.choice: included
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

en.B: Allammelech, Amad and Mishal. On the west it reaches Carmel and Shihor-libnath.
en.R: Allammelech, Amad and Mishal. On the west, the border reached Mount Carmel and Shihor-libnath.

sw.L: na Alameleki, na Amadi, na Mishali. Na unagusa Karmeli kuelekea magharibi, na Shihori-libnathi.
sw.B: Alameleki, Amadi na Mishali. Upande wa magharibi unafika Karmeli na Shihori-libnathi.
sw.R: Alameleki, Amadi na Mishali. Upande wa magharibi, mpaka ulifika Mlima Karmeli na Shihori-libnathi.

es.B: Alamelec, Amad y Miseal. Por el occidente llega al Carmelo y a Sihor-libnat.
es.R: Alamelec, Amad y Miseal. Por el oeste, la frontera llegaba al monte Carmelo y a Sihor-libnat.

decisions.choice: Carmel and Shihor-libnath on the west
decisions.reason: Carmel is the mountain ridge that runs out to the sea, the place of Elijah's contest (1 Kings 18:19-20). Shihor-libnath was probably a stream near it; its site is not known, and the first part of the name is used of a river elsewhere (13:3).

decisions.choice: Mount Carmel; the border
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Mount" and names "the border" as the subject, which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

records.literal_gloss: And turns back [toward the] rising of the sun [to] Beth-dagon, and touches on Zebulun, and on [the] valley of Iphtah-el northward, [and] Beth-emek and Neiel; and goes out to Cabul on [the] left,

en.L: And it turns toward the sunrise to Beth-dagon, and touches Zebulun, and the valley of Iphtah-el northward, Beth-emek, and Neiel, and goes out to Cabul on the left,
en.B: Then it turns east toward the sunrise to Beth-dagon, reaches Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el to the north, Beth-emek and Neiel, and goes on to Cabul on the north,
en.R: Then the border turned east to Beth-dagon. It reached the land of Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el to the north, and Beth-emek and Neiel. Then it went north to Cabul,

sw.L: Na unageuka kuelekea mawio ya jua hadi Beth-dagoni, na kugusa Zabuloni, na bonde la Ifta-eli kuelekea kaskazini, Beth-emeki, na Neieli, na kutokea Kabuli upande wa kushoto,
sw.B: Kisha unageuka mashariki kuelekea mawio ya jua hadi Beth-dagoni, unafika Zabuloni na bonde la Ifta-eli upande wa kaskazini, Beth-emeki na Neieli, na kuendelea hadi Kabuli upande wa kaskazini,
sw.R: Kisha mpaka uligeuka mashariki hadi Beth-dagoni. Ulifika nchi ya Zabuloni na bonde la Ifta-eli upande wa kaskazini, na Beth-emeki na Neieli. Kisha ukaenda kaskazini hadi Kabuli,

es.L: Y gira hacia la salida del sol a Bet-dagón, y toca Zabulón, y el valle de Jefte-el al norte, Bet-emec, y Neiel, y sale a Cabul a la izquierda,
es.B: Luego gira al oriente, hacia la salida del sol, hasta Bet-dagón, llega a Zabulón y al valle de Jefte-el por el norte, a Bet-emec y Neiel, y sigue hasta Cabul por el norte,
es.R: Luego la frontera giraba al este hasta Bet-dagón. Llegaba a la tierra de Zabulón y al valle de Jefte-el por el norte, y a Bet-emec y Neiel. Después iba al norte hasta Cabul,

decisions.choice: on the left: on the north
decisions.reason: Directions were given facing the sunrise, so the left hand was the north and the right hand the south (Genesis 14:15).

decisions.choice: Beth-dagon and Cabul
decisions.reason: Beth-dagon means "house of Dagon", a god worshiped on the coast (Judges 16:23); this is not the town of the same name in Judah (15:41). Cabul was among the towns Solomon later gave to Hiram king of Tyre (1 Kings 9:11-13).

decisions.choice: on the north / went north
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "north" for "left", as the meaning decision explains. Literal keeps "on the left".

decisions.choice: "a la izquierda" (L); "por el norte" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew names the north as "the left hand", facing east. Literal keeps the word; Balanced and Readable say "north", as the English does. The Carmel is "el Carmelo", its usual Spanish name.

records.literal_gloss: and Ebron and Rehob and Hammon and Kanah, as far as Sidon [the] great.

en.L: and Ebron, and Rehob, and Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Sidon the great.
en.B: Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as great Sidon.
en.R: and on to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as the great city of Sidon.

sw.L: na Ebroni, na Rehobu, na Hamoni, na Kana, hadi Sidoni Kuu.
sw.B: Ebroni, Rehobu, Hamoni na Kana, hadi Sidoni Kuu.
sw.R: na kuendelea hadi Ebroni, Rehobu, Hamoni na Kana, hadi mji mkuu wa Sidoni.

es.L: y Ebrón, y Rehob, y Hamón, y Caná, hasta Sidón la grande.
es.B: Ebrón, Rehob, Hamón y Caná, hasta la gran Sidón.
es.R: y seguía hasta Ebrón, Rehob, Hamón y Caná, hasta la gran ciudad de Sidón.

decisions.choice: Ebron: kept as in the Hebrew text; many manuscripts read Abdon
decisions.reason: Many Hebrew manuscripts have "Abdon", the name of the Levite town of Asher (21:30; 1 Chronicles 6:59). In Hebrew writing the letters for d and r look very much alike, so one name could easily become the other. The text followed here has Ebron.

decisions.choice: great Sidon: the leading city of the Phoenician coast
decisions.reason: Sidon was the chief city of the coast north of Tyre; "great" probably takes in the lands around it (11:8). The border ran toward its territory, but Asher never drove out its people (Judges 1:31).

source.text: וְשָׁ֤ב הַגְּבוּל֙ הָֽרָמָ֔ה וְעַד־עִ֖יר מִבְצַר־צֹ֑ר וְשָׁ֤ב הַגְּבוּל֙ חֹסָ֔ה וְהָי֧וּ תֹצְאֹתָ֛יו הַיָּ֖מָּה מֵחֶ֥בֶל אַכְזִֽיבָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And turns back the border [to] the Ramah and to [the] city of fortification of Tyre; and turns back the border [to] Hosah, and were its ends at the sea, from [the] region toward Achzib,

en.L: And the border turns to Ramah, and to the fortified city of Tyre, and the border turns to Hosah, and its end is at the sea, from the region toward Achzib,
en.B: Then the border turns to Ramah and on to the fortified city of Tyre. It turns to Hosah and ends at the sea, in the district of Achzib,
en.R: Then the border turned to Ramah and to the walled city of Tyre. It turned to Hosah and ended at the sea, in the area of Achzib.

sw.L: Na mpaka unageuka hadi Rama, na hadi mji wenye ngome wa Tiro, na mpaka unageuka hadi Hosa, na mwisho wake ni baharini, kutoka eneo kuelekea Akzibu,
sw.B: Kisha mpaka unageuka hadi Rama na kuendelea hadi mji wenye ngome wa Tiro. Unageuka hadi Hosa na kuishia baharini, katika eneo la Akzibu,
sw.R: Kisha mpaka uligeuka hadi Rama na hadi mji wenye kuta wa Tiro. Ukageuka hadi Hosa, ukaishia baharini, katika eneo la Akzibu.

es.L: Y gira la frontera hacia Ramá, y hasta la ciudad fortificada de Tiro, y gira la frontera hacia Hosa, y sus salidas están en el mar, desde la región hacia Aczib,
es.B: Luego la frontera gira hacia Ramá y sigue hasta la ciudad fortificada de Tiro. Gira hacia Hosa y termina en el mar, en el distrito de Aczib,
es.R: Después la frontera giraba hacia Ramá y hasta la ciudad amurallada de Tiro. Giraba hacia Hosa y terminaba en el mar, en la zona de Aczib.

decisions.choice: the fortified city of Tyre
decisions.reason: Tyre was a strong Phoenician port, built on an island just off the coast with a town on the shore. Asher's border ran near it, but Tyre was never Israel's (2 Samuel 24:7 calls it a stronghold).

decisions.choice: from the region toward Achzib: the area around Achzib
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and hard. The word after "from" usually means a measured stretch of land, so the phrase most likely places the end of the border near Achzib, a town on the coast south of Tyre (Judges 1:31). The same letters can also be read as the name of a town, Mahalab, which ancient Assyrian records place on this coast; the line would then run "from Mahalab to Achzib".

decisions.choice: ends the sentence here
decisions.reason: Readable closes the sentence at Achzib and gives the last towns and the total in verse 30 as a sentence of their own. Literal and Balanced run on into verse 30.

en.R: Ummah, Aphek and Rehob were also theirs. In all, there were twenty-two towns with their villages.

sw.B: na pia Uma, Afeki na Rehobu: miji ishirini na miwili pamoja na vijiji vyake.
sw.R: Uma, Afeki na Rehobu ilikuwa yao pia. Kwa jumla ilikuwa miji ishirini na miwili pamoja na vijiji vyake.

es.B: y además Uma, Afec y Rehob: veintidós poblaciones y sus aldeas.
es.R: Uma, Afec y Rehob también eran suyos. En total, eran veintidós pueblos con sus aldeas.

decisions.choice: twenty-two: the total
decisions.reason: As with Zebulun (verse 15), the total takes in towns named along the border, and how the count was made is no longer certain.

decisions.choice: Aphek and Rehob in Asher
decisions.reason: This Aphek is not the town of the same name in the south (12:18). Rehob is also named in verse 28; there may have been two towns called Rehob. Judges 1:31 names both among the towns whose people Asher did not drive out.

decisions.choice: and also / were also theirs
decisions.reason: These names add to Asher's list of towns. Balanced and Readable add words to show it, as in verse 7.

decisions.reason: As in verse 8: the summary that ends each tribe's allotment.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Asher; share of land
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

es.R: La sexta suerte se echó para la tribu de Neftalí, clan por clan.

decisions.choice: the tribe named first
decisions.reason: As in verse 17. Naphtali's land was eastern and upper Galilee, west of the Jordan and the Sea of Chinnereth.

decisions.choice: The sixth lot came out for the tribe of Naphtali, clan by clan.
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

en.L: And their border was from Heleph, from the great tree in Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb, and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and its end is at the Jordan.
en.B: Their border runs from Heleph, from the great tree at Zaanannim, by Adami-nekeb and Jabneel as far as Lakkum, and it ends at the Jordan.

sw.L: Na mpaka wao ulikuwa kutoka Helefu, kutoka mti mkubwa ulioko Saananimu, na Adami-nekebu, na Yabneeli, hadi Lakumu, na mwisho wake ni Yordani.
sw.B: Mpaka wao unaanzia Helefu, kutoka mti mkubwa ulioko Saananimu, kupitia Adami-nekebu na Yabneeli hadi Lakumu, na kuishia Yordani.
sw.R: Mpaka wao ulianzia Helefu na mti mkubwa ulioko Saananimu, ukapita Adami-nekebu na Yabneeli, hadi Lakumu. Uliishia Mto Yordani.

es.L: Y su frontera fue desde Helef, desde el gran árbol de Saananim, y Adami-neceb, y Jabneel, hasta Lacum, y sus salidas están en el Jordán.
es.B: Su frontera va desde Helef, desde el gran árbol de Saananim, por Adami-neceb y Jabneel hasta Lacum, y termina en el Jordán.
es.R: Su frontera iba desde Helef y el gran árbol de Saananim, pasando por Adami-neceb y Jabneel, hasta Lacum. Terminaba en el río Jordán.

decisions.choice: the great tree: a large oak or terebinth that marked the place
decisions.reason: The word names a large, long-lived tree, often a landmark or a place of worship (Genesis 12:6; 13:18). Which kind of tree is not certain. The words have also been read as the name of a place, Elon-bezaanannim.

decisions.choice: the tree in Zaanannim: where Heber the Kenite camped
decisions.reason: Judges 4:11 says Heber pitched his tent "as far as the great tree in Zaanannim, near Kedesh". It was near his tent that Sisera died (Judges 4:17-21).

decisions.choice: great tree
decisions.reason: All three levels say "great tree", not "oak", because the kind of tree is not certain.

decisions.choice: "el gran árbol"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a large, notable tree whose kind is not certain; Spanish says "el gran árbol", as the English says "great tree", rather than naming a kind of oak.

records.literal_gloss: And turns back the border westward [to] Aznoth-tabor, and goes out from there to Hukkok; and touches on Zebulun from [the] south, and on Asher touches from [the] west, and on Judah [at] the Jordan [toward the] rising of the sun.

en.L: And the border turns westward to Aznoth-tabor, and goes out from there to Hukkok, and touches Zebulun on the south, and touches Asher on the west, and Judah [at] the Jordan toward the sunrise.
en.B: Then the border turns west to Aznoth-tabor and goes on from there to Hukkok. It reaches Zebulun on the south and Asher on the west, and on the east it reaches Judah at the Jordan.
en.R: Then the border turned west to Aznoth-tabor and went on to Hukkok. It reached the land of Zebulun on the south and the land of Asher on the west. On the east it reached Judah at the Jordan River.

sw.L: Na mpaka unageuka kuelekea magharibi hadi Aznoth-tabori, na kutokea huko hadi Hukoki, na kugusa Zabuloni upande wa kusini, na kugusa Asheri upande wa magharibi, na Yuda [kwenye] Yordani kuelekea mawio ya jua.
sw.B: Kisha mpaka unageuka magharibi hadi Aznoth-tabori na kuendelea kutoka huko hadi Hukoki. Unafika Zabuloni upande wa kusini na Asheri upande wa magharibi, na upande wa mashariki unafika Yuda kwenye Yordani.

decisions.choice: the territory went out from them: the land slipped out of their control
alternatives: the territory of the Danites went out beyond these towns
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean that Dan's land was lost to them, as Judges 1:34 tells: the Amorites forced the Danites into the hills and kept them from the plain. They can also mean that the territory reached out beyond the towns just listed. The ancient Greek translation reads differently again, saying that the Danites did not drive out the Amorites who pressed them. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek translation and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: Leshem renamed Dan: the story of Judges 18
decisions.reason: Leshem is the Laish of Judges 18, a quiet town far to the north near the springs of the Jordan. Judges 18 tells how the Danites sent spies, attacked it and renamed it Dan. This note looks ahead to events after the time of the allotments; the town later marks Israel's northern limit, "from Dan to Beersheba" (Judges 20:1).

decisions.choice: struck it to the mouth of the sword: killed its people with the sword
decisions.reason: The sword is pictured as a mouth that devours (Deuteronomy 32:42). "Struck it" means the town's people (Judges 18:27).

decisions.choice: Dan their father: Jacob's son, the tribe's ancestor
decisions.reason: Dan was the son of Jacob and Bilhah (Genesis 30:6), from whom the tribe was descended.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dan / the Danites
decisions.reason: Literal gives the first "sons of Dan", the tribe whose land it was, with the gender setting; the second names the men who went to war, so it has no setting. Balanced and Readable say "the Danites" for both.

decisions.choice: went north
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "went up". Readable says "went north", since Leshem lay in the far north (Judges 18:7, 29), and "killed its people" for "struck it".

decisions.choice: "a filo de espada" (L, B); "a espada" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to the mouth of the sword". Spanish has its own fixed phrase for the same picture, "a filo de espada" ("by the edge of the sword"), which Literal and Balanced use; Readable says it plainly. Literal "se les salió de las manos" renders "went out from them" as the meaning decisions read it, the land slipping from their control.

decisions.choice: "los danitas" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "los danitas", the people of the tribe of Dan, as the English says "the Danites"; Literal keeps "los hijos de Dan".

sw.R: Hii ndiyo sehemu ya nchi ambayo kabila la Dani lilipokea, ukoo kwa ukoo: miji hiyo na vijiji vyake.

es.L: Esta [es] la heredad de la tribu de los hijos de Dan conforme a sus clanes, estas ciudades y sus aldeas.
es.B: Esta fue la heredad de la tribu de Dan, clan por clan: estas poblaciones y sus aldeas.
es.R: Esta fue la parte de la tierra que recibió la tribu de Dan, clan por clan: estos pueblos y sus aldeas.

decisions.choice: the closing words of the tribe's section
decisions.reason: As in verse 8: the summary that ends each tribe's allotment. It closes the list of verses 41-46, after the note of verse 47.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Dan; share of land
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: וַיְכַלּ֥וּ לִנְחֹל־אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לִגְבֽוּלֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל נַחֲלָ֛ה לִיהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בִּן־נ֖וּן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they finished dividing for inheritance the land by its borders; and gave [the] sons of Israel an inheritance to Joshua son of Nun in their midst.

en.L: And they finished dividing the land for inheritance by its borders, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua son of Nun in their midst.
en.B: When they had finished dividing up the land as inheritances by its borders, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
en.R: When all the land had been divided up, each part within its borders, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave Joshua son of Nun a share of land among them.

sw.L: Na wakamaliza kuigawa nchi kuwa urithi kwa mipaka yake, na wana wa Israeli wakampa Yoshua mwana wa Nuni urithi katikati yao.
sw.B: Walipokwisha kuigawa nchi kuwa urithi kwa mipaka yake, Waisraeli walimpa Yoshua mwana wa Nuni urithi kati yao.
sw.R: Nchi yote ilipokwisha kugawanywa, kila sehemu ndani ya mipaka yake, Waisraeli walimpa Yoshua mwana wa Nuni sehemu ya nchi kati yao.

es.L: Y terminaron de repartir la tierra en heredad por sus fronteras, y los hijos de Israel dieron heredad a Josué hijo de Nun en medio de ellos.
es.B: Cuando terminaron de repartir la tierra en heredades según sus fronteras, los israelitas dieron a Josué hijo de Nun una heredad entre ellos.
es.R: Cuando toda la tierra quedó repartida, cada parte dentro de sus fronteras, los israelitas le dieron a Josué hijo de Nun una parte de la tierra entre ellos.

decisions.choice: dividing for inheritance: handing out the land as lasting possessions
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "inheritance". It means to give out land as property that each tribe and family would keep.

decisions.choice: Joshua receives his share last
decisions.reason: The leader is given his own land only after every tribe has received its share. Caleb, the other faithful spy, had also received his land by promise (14:6-15).

decisions.choice: When they had finished ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the first clause a time clause, since the gift to Joshua comes after the division is done.

source.text: עַל־פִּ֨י יְהוָ֜ה נָ֣תְנוּ ל֗וֹ אֶת־הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔ל אֶת־תִּמְנַת־סֶ֖רַח בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיִּבְנֶ֥ה אֶת־הָעִ֖יר וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: At [the] mouth of Yahweh they gave to him the city which he asked, Timnath-serah in [the] hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city and lived in it.

en.L: At the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they gave him the city that he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and he built the city and lived in it.
en.B: At the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they gave him the town he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He built up the town and settled there.
en.R: As {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded, they gave him the town he asked for. It was Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. Joshua built up the town and lived there.

sw.L: Kwa kinywa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakampa mji aliouomba, Timnath-sera katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, naye akaujenga mji akakaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Kwa agizo la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} walimpa mji aliouomba, Timnath-sera katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu. Aliujenga upya mji huo, akakaa humo.
sw.R: Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameamuru, walimpa mji aliouomba. Ulikuwa Timnath-sera katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu. Yoshua aliujenga upya mji huo, akaishi humo.

es.L: Conforme a la boca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dieron la ciudad que pidió, Timnat-sera, en la región montañosa de Efraín; y él edificó la ciudad y habitó en ella.
es.B: Por orden {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dieron la población que pidió, Timnat-sera, en la región montañosa de Efraín. Él reconstruyó la población y se estableció allí.
es.R: Tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado, le dieron el pueblo que pidió. Era Timnat-sera, en la región montañosa de Efraín. Josué reconstruyó el pueblo y vivió allí.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of the LORD: by the LORD's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says. The phrase means "at the LORD's word" or "by his order" (Numbers 3:16; 9:18). The command itself is not recorded; Joshua, like Caleb, had been promised that he would enter the land (Numbers 14:30).

decisions.choice: Timnath-serah in Ephraim
decisions.reason: Joshua belonged to the tribe of Ephraim (Numbers 13:8). He was buried in this town (24:30), which Judges 2:9 calls Timnath-heres.

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt or strengthened
decisions.reason: The verb can mean building a town anew or building up one that already stood, by repairing and fortifying it.

decisions.choice: built up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "built up", which fits either sense; Literal keeps "built".

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה הַנְּחָלֹ֡ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִחֲל֣וּ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֣ן׀וִיהוֹשֻׁ֪עַ בִּן־נ֟וּן וְרָאשֵׁ֣י הָֽאָב֣וֹת לְמַטּוֹת֩ בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל׀בְּגוֹרָ֤ל׀בְּשִׁלֹה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיְכַלּ֕וּ מֵֽחַלֵּ֖ק אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: These [are] the inheritances which gave as possession Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and [the] heads of the fathers of [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel by lot in Shiloh before Yahweh, [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting; and they finished from dividing the land.

en.L: These [are] the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, and Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave as possessions by lot in Shiloh before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. And they finished dividing the land.
en.B: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family heads of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} handed out these inheritances by lot at Shiloh, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
en.R: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the family leaders of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave out these shares of land. They drew lots at Shiloh, in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the meeting tent. So they finished dividing up the land.

sw.L: Hii [ndiyo] mirathi ambayo Eleazari kuhani, na Yoshua mwana wa Nuni, na wakuu wa baba wa makabila ya wana wa Israeli waliigawa kuwa milki kwa kura huko Shilo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania. Nao wakamaliza kuigawa nchi.
sw.B: Eleazari kuhani, Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na wakuu wa jamaa za makabila ya Waisraeli waligawa mirathi hii kwa kura huko Shilo, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania. Hivyo wakamaliza kuigawa nchi.
sw.R: Eleazari kuhani, Yoshua mwana wa Nuni na viongozi wa jamaa za makabila ya Waisraeli waligawa sehemu hizi za nchi. Walipiga kura huko Shilo, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania. Hivyo wakamaliza kuigawa nchi.

es.L: Estas [son] las heredades que el sacerdote Eleazar, y Josué hijo de Nun, y las cabezas de los padres de las tribus de los hijos de Israel repartieron por suerte en Silo delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro. Y terminaron de repartir la tierra.
es.B: El sacerdote Eleazar, Josué hijo de Nun y los jefes de familia de las tribus de los israelitas repartieron estas heredades por suerte en Silo, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro. Así terminaron de repartir la tierra.
es.R: El sacerdote Eleazar, Josué hijo de Nun y los jefes de las familias de las tribus de los israelitas repartieron estas partes de la tierra. Echaron suertes en Silo, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro. Así terminaron de repartir la tierra.

decisions.choice: Eleazar, Joshua and the family heads: the leaders named for this task
decisions.reason: The LORD had named these leaders to divide the land: Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and one leader from each tribe (Numbers 34:16-29). The same group is named when the dividing begins (14:1).

decisions.choice: at Shiloh, before the LORD, at the tent of meeting
decisions.reason: The tent of meeting had been set up at Shiloh (18:1). To cast lots "before the LORD" at its entrance was to leave the outcome to him in his presence (18:6, 8, 10).

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the family lines within a tribe; their heads were the tribe's leaders (Numbers 32:28).

decisions.choice: and they finished dividing the land: the close of the whole division
decisions.reason: The words repeat the start of verse 49 and close the account of the dividing of the land that began in 14:1.

decisions.choice: family heads / family leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "families" for "fathers", following the meaning decision; Literal keeps "fathers".
